description: Find layout slips that read as mistakes. Pass `boxes` (array or JSON string of {x, y, w, h, label}, 2 to 400 boxes) or `html` plus optional `css`. For markup, geometry comes from data-x, data-y, data-w, data-h attributes or from left, top, width and height in px (inline style, or simple .class, #id and tag rules in `css`); elements without all four are skipped and counted. Nothing is rendered, so this reads declared numbers only. Reports (1) near-misses: left, right, top, bottom or center lines of two boxes that differ by more than 0.01px and no more than `tolerance` (default 6px), with both values and the difference; (2) inconsistent gaps between three or more siblings that share a row or column, listing every gap and the most common one; (3) orphans, boxes that line up with nothing and sit more than twice the median nearest-neighbor distance away. Sources: Müller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design (alignment to a shared structure); Lupton, Thinking with Type (alignment and grouping); Wroblewski, Web Form Design (labels close to their fields). The tolerance and orphan thresholds are conventions. Pure arithmetic, nothing stored.

boxes.description: Boxes as {x, y, w, h, label}. A JSON string is also accepted.

css.description: CSS for the markup (simple class, id and tag selectors).

html.description: Markup with positioned elements (alternative to boxes).
